A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ArgSum systems and evaluation framework. All 20 pages of v1 and 21 pages of v3, including appendices and visual material, support comparison. The placeholder in v1 Appendix B.3 is a document omission, not an extraction gap.

before.justification: v1 reports original human annotations, metric correlations, clustering evaluations, and argument summarization results on ArgKP21 and Debate.

after.justification: v3 retains the original human evaluation and metric results and reports summarization experiments using four LLMs on ArgKP21 and Debate.

M1.justification: The MCArgSum clustering and summarization procedure, fine-tuning, LLM integration strategies, and evaluator definitions remain unchanged. Additional LLM configurations and the newly documented evaluation prompts do not establish an algorithmic revision.

E1.justification: ArgQ, ArgKP21 and Debate remain the training and evaluation resources, with the same topic/stance-conditioned argument summarization setting. The added models and removal of the clustering-stage diagnostic do not change the represented data or input scenarios.

E2.justification: Tables 2 and 8 in v3 expand the comparisons to LLaMA-3.3-70B, Qwen2.5-72B and Qwen3-32B variants alongside GPT-4o. Conversely, the separate comparisons involving MCArgSum with BarH/SMatchToPr scorers and USKPM iterative clustering disappear with v1's clustering study. The original summarization and automatic-metric baselines remain.

E3.justification: v3 adds three LLM configurations, including Qwen3-32B in non-thinking mode, under shared prompts and parameter settings. It removes the ARI evaluation protocol, including best-clustering selection, the greater-than-70% clustered requirement, and alternative noise treatments. Retained preprocessing, sample counts and weighted-score evaluation remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v1 Section 4.2.1 and Tables 7–8 investigate match-scorer substitutions, noise handling and iterative clustering through clustering quality and runtime. This entire component analysis is removed. v3 Section 4.2 adds qualitative inspection comparing terse LLaMA summaries with fuller Qwen and GPT-4o outputs.

E5.justification: Both versions average 10 LLM evaluation runs and retain the same annotator-correlation analysis and standard-deviation reporting for metric correlations. Added summarization configurations use the existing point-estimate reporting practice. No independent change to seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance testing is reported.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial results for three LLMs: BarH+summ(Qwen3-32B) leads with weighted scores of 0.925 on ArgKP21 and 0.900 on Debate, while MCArgSum(LLaMA-3.3-70B) scores 0.765 and 0.729. Retained GPT-4o and baseline scores agree with v1 Figure 2 at its displayed precision. The ARI and clustering-runtime results are removed.

T1.justification: Equations 1–4 and their mathematical content remain unchanged. Neither version contains substantive theoretical proofs. Removing the descriptive ARI evaluation passage changes the experimental protocol rather than formal theory.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction add a central contribution concerning Qwen3-32B outperforming GPT-4o and LLaMA-3.3-70B underperforming. The conclusion replaces MCArgSum's dataset-specific highest-performance claim with a broader claim of outperforming existing approaches and adds a Qwen-based state-of-the-art claim.

C2.justification: The discussion shifts from generally favoring candidate generation and MCArgSum on Debate to model-dependent gains and stronger summary-generation configurations. It attributes weak LLaMA results to short summaries and adds limitations concerning GPT-oriented prompts and missing human validation of open-source outputs. The clustering accuracy/runtime interpretation is removed.

D1.justification: Appendix B.3 changes from an ellipsis to full evaluator prompts, worked examples, output formats and input-formatting instructions. v3 also documents BarH candidate filters and OpenRouter access. However, the dated GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini snapshot identifiers disappear. Existing fine-tuning, hardware and generation-prompt details remain.

R1.justification: v3 adds the LLaMA 3, Qwen2.5 and Qwen3 technical-report references and removes Warrens and van der Hoef's ARI reference. Section 2 and the positioning as the first systematic integration study remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: Editing concentrates on the contribution list, system-results discussion, conclusion and limitations. Section 4.2's two subsections become one section, and author/affiliation information changes. The overall organization and most method, metric and existing appendix prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v1 Figure 2's summarization bar charts are replaced by a main-text weighted-score table and an expanded appendix table. The two clustering tables and two ARI figures are removed. Figure 1 moves from a two-column placement to a smaller single-column display, substantially changing the presentation of results and supporting visuals.

improvement.justification: Completing Appendix B.3 closes an important documentation gap, while the additional LLM comparisons reveal model-dependent failures beyond v1's GPT-4o-only evidence. Explicit prompt-bias and human-validation limitations improve interpretability. These gains are tempered by removal of the clustering study supporting MCArgSum and loss of exact GPT snapshot identifiers, yielding a limited overall improvement.
